title: How to Migrate an Existing Project to Vite+
summary: Migrate an existing project to Vite+ with vp migrate. Check prerequisites, review converted configs and hooks, verify builds and tests, and update CI safely.
body_markdown:
To migrate an existing project to Vite+, run` vp migrate` at the project or workspace root on a fresh branch. Read the plan it prints before any files change, then confirm the result with` vp install` ,` vp check` ,` vp test` and` vp build` (or` vp pack` for a library) before you update CI.


Moving a working repo with five separate tool configs onto a new toolchain is the kind of change that looks small in a PR title and then takes up a full sprint. Usually the trouble starts once the automated part has finished, in what it did and didn’t convert.


This guide is for projects that already run Vite, Vitest, ESLint and Prettier. It covers what` vp migrate` changes, what it leaves for you, what to check afterwards, and how to update GitHub Actions and GitLab CI. If you need an overview of Vite+ and its commands first, start with[Getting Started with Vite+](https://blog.openreplay.com/getting-started-vite/) .[Vite+ 1.0 shipped on 28 September 2026](https://voidzero.dev/posts/announcing-vite-plus-1-0) under the MIT license.


## Key Takeaways


- Projects not yet on Vite+ need Vite 7+ and Vitest 4+ before running` vp migrate` , and the Vite+ CLI requires Node.js` ^22.18.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0` .
- In a monorepo, run` vp migrate` once at the workspace root, because lockfiles, catalogs and package-manager settings are shared across packages.
- ` vp migrate` leaves Husky, lefthook, simple-git-hooks and yorkie in place and prints a warning instead of converting them.
- On GitHub Actions, a single` voidzero-dev/setup-vp` step with` node-version` and` cache: true` replaces separate Node, package-manager, install and cache steps.
- Pin setup-vp to an exact release tag or commit SHA, because the floating` v1` tag no longer receives updates.


## Who Should Migrate to Vite+ and What Do You Get?


Migrating suits teams that maintain separate configs for Vite, Vitest, ESLint, Prettier and a library bundler such as tsup or tsdown. After migration you have one` vite-plus` dependency and one` vite.config.ts` that holds dev, test, lint, format and pack settings. tsup is a[supported migration source](https://viteplus.dev/guide/migrate-rules) , so a TypeScript library that bundles with tsup can come across too. Expect follow-up work, though. The[migration guide](https://viteplus.dev/guide/migrate) states plainly that most projects need some manual adjustment once the command finishes.


## What Do You Need Before Running vp migrate?


Run the Vite+ migration on its own branch, starting from a clean working tree. That way the diff contains only migration changes and is easy to throw away.


```text
git   switch   -c   chore/migrate-vite-plus
git   status     # should report a clean tree
```


Check these three things before you start:


- **Vite 7 or later.** Older projects need to upgrade Vite first.[What’s New in Vite 7](https://blog.openreplay.com/whats-new-vite-7-rust-baseline-beyond/) covers the changes in that release.
- **Vitest 4 or later.** Upgrade older suites to v4 before migrating.
- **Node.js` ^22.18.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0`** , per the[Vitest 5 upgrade guide](https://viteplus.dev/guide/vitest-v5) .


Do any upstream upgrades first and validate them, then keep the existing lockfile and installed packages. The migrator reads them to work out which Vitest version you started from.


## Run vp migrate and Read the Plan


Running` vp migrate` with no arguments migrates the current directory. It shows the planned changes before it writes any files. Pass a path to migrate a project in another directory.


```text
vp   migrate                      # interactive, migrates the current directory
vp   migrate   ./path/to/project    # migrate another directory
vp   migrate   --no-interactive     # scripted runs
```


The migrate command accepts these flags:


- ` --no-interactive` runs without prompts.
- ` --agent <name>` /` --no-agent` controls whether coding-agent instruction files are set up.
- ` --editor <name>` /` --no-editor` controls whether editor configuration is written.
- ` --hooks` /` --no-hooks` controls whether git hooks are set up.


In a monorepo, the workspace root is the only valid target for` vp migrate` . The lockfiles, catalogs and package-manager settings it rewrites belong to every package in the workspace, so run it once from the root. Don’t run it package by package.


## What Does vp migrate Convert and What Does It Leave Alone?


` vp migrate` updates dependencies, rewrites imports, merges tool configuration into` vite.config.ts` , updates` package.json` scripts and formats the files it changed. It deliberately leaves existing git-hook tools untouched.


Item What happens


Dependencies, imports, scripts Converted


Oxlint, Oxfmt and JSON lint-staged config Merged into` vite.config.ts`


tsdown config Brought into the` pack` block of` vite.config.ts`


ESLint flat config, Prettier config Converted to Oxlint/Oxfmt settings and merged; old packages, configs and scripts are replaced


Legacy` .eslintrc` Left in place, along with ESLint and its lint script


lint-staged (JSON config) Moved to a` staged` block if no hook tool is kept


Non-JSON` .lintstagedrc` ,` lint-staged.config.*` Not migrated automatically


Husky Left as-is, with a warning


lefthook, simple-git-hooks, yorkie Left as-is, with a warning, even when you pass` --hooks`


` declare module 'vitest'` Left as-is on purpose


Test imports switch from upstream Vitest to the re-exports in` vite-plus` , which bundles Vitest 5. Type augmentations still target upstream` vitest` :


```text
// before
import   {   defineConfig   }   from   '  vitest/config  '
import   {   describe  ,   it  ,   expect   }   from   '  vitest  '


// after
import   {   defineConfig   }   from   '  vite-plus  '
import   {   describe  ,   it  ,   expect   }   from   '  vite-plus/test  '


declare   module   '  vitest  '   {
// unchanged: augmentations keep targeting upstream vitest
}
```


If you keep a hook tool, lint-staged stays too, because` vp staged` reads only the` staged` block in` vite.config.ts` . You switch to it by hand:


```text
import   {   defineConfig   }   from   '  vite-plus  '


export default   defineConfig  ({
staged  :   {
'  *.{js,ts,tsx}  '  :   '  vp check --fix  '  ,
},
})
```


For libraries on tsdown older than 0.23 (or when the installed version can’t be found), the migration keeps the old defaults. It adds` deps.resolveDepSubpath: true` to the` pack` block if you haven’t set it, and adds` attw.profile: 'strict'` if ATTW checks are on and no profile is set. The migration rules list the full set of transformations.


## How Do You Verify the Migrated Project?


Run` vp install` ,` vp check` ,` vp test` and` vp build` (or` vp pack` for a library), and review each result before you commit. Because the migration runs the formatter over the files it changed, review the formatting changes separately from the dependency, config and import changes. Otherwise a reformatting diff can hide logic changes.


Command What to inspect


` vp install` Lockfile changes


` vp check` New lint and format findings


` vp test` Test results; for v4 configs, the compatibility settings added for options you hadn’t set


` vp build` /` vp pack` Output files; for libraries, emitted imports, declarations and the tsdown compatibility settings


Read the review report the migration writes before you commit. If you run browser-mode, coverage or benchmark suites, run them separately as well.


## What If Lint or Format Rules Don’t Carry Over?


The migration converts ESLint flat config to Oxlint and Prettier config to Oxfmt where it can, but not every ESLint rule has an Oxlint equivalent.` vp migrate` lists the unsupported rules it skips. If a rule you depend on doesn’t come across, keep the original tool as a project script and run it through` vp run` :


```text
{   "  scripts  "  : {   "  lint:eslint  "  :   "  eslint .  "   } }
```


```text
vp   run   lint:eslint
```


This only works if the ESLint script survives the migration. That happens if you declined the ESLint/Prettier conversion prompt or have a legacy` .eslintrc` . Otherwise, add the package, config and script back yourself after migrating. Note that` vp test` always runs the built-in test command, while` vp run test` runs whatever` test` script is in` package.json` .


If Node or the package manager resolves to the wrong version, run` vp env doctor` to diagnose it.


## How Do You Update CI for Vite+?


In CI, the Vite+ setup action replaces the separate Node, package manager, install and cache steps, and the jobs call the` vp` commands directly. On GitHub Actions,[setup-vp](https://github.com/voidzero-dev/setup-vp) installs dependencies unless you set` run-install: false` :


```text
name  :   CI
on  :
push  :
branches  : [  main  ]
pull_request  :


jobs  :
check  :
runs-on  :   ubuntu-latest
steps  :
-   uses  :   actions/checkout@v7
-   uses  :   voidzero-dev/setup-vp@<setup-vp-version>
with  :
node-version  :   '  24  '
cache  :   true
-   run  :   vp check
-   run  :   vp test
-   run  :   vp build
```


On GitLab, the[CI guide](https://viteplus.dev/guide/ci) has you include the remote` setup-vp.yml` template, extend` .setup-vp` and use an image that already contains Node:


```text
include  :
# copy the exact remote URL from the Vite+ CI guide
-   remote  :   '  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/voidzero-dev/setup-vp/<setup-vp-version>/gitlab/setup-vp.yml  '
inputs  :
setup-ref  :   '  <setup-vp-version>  '


check  :
extends  :   .setup-vp
image  :   node:24
# caching uses GitLab's native cache: keyword
script  :
-   vp check
-   vp test
-   vp build
```


Pin setup-vp to an exact release tag or commit SHA rather than` v1` , because VoidZero no longer updates that tag. Search your workflows for` setup-vp@v1` and replace it. On GitLab, the version appears twice (once in the include URL and once in` setup-ref` ), and you need to update both by hand when you upgrade.


## Conclusion


A Vite+ migration goes smoothly when you treat` vp migrate` as the first step rather than the whole job. Read its plan, keep formatting changes apart from logic changes, run the four verification commands, and pin setup-vp in CI before you merge. Next, open the branch, run` vp migrate` , and go through the warnings it prints for hooks and lint rules.


## FAQs


What does vp migrate do on a project that already uses Vite+?


It only upgrades the toolchain. It updates dependencies and package-manager settings across every workspace package to the versions bundled with the CLI running the migration, and finalizes imports. It skips first-time setup such as git hooks, editor and agent files, and lint migration. Pass --full to also run those setup actions. Run vp upgrade first so the global CLI has the latest migration rules.


Should I run vp migrate from the project's own node_modules?


No. The Vite+ migration guide says not to run migration with an old project's node_modules/.bin/vp. Use a global vp, or fetch the target release with npx --package=vite-plus@version vp migrate or the pnpm dlx equivalent. This loads the target CLI without replacing the project's old dependencies first, so the migrator can still detect which Vitest version you started from.


Which package managers does Vite+ support after migration?


Vite+ works with pnpm, npm, Yarn and Bun. It detects the package manager from files at the workspace root, such as the packageManager field and the lockfile, and falls back to pnpm if it finds none. vp install then runs the matching install behaviour for the detected manager, including the correct lockfile flags.


How do I find out which ESLint rules the migration dropped?


vp migrate reports the unsupported ESLint rules it skips during conversion to Oxlint. This arrived in Vite+ 0.3.2 so you can review the checks you lose. Go through that list before you commit, then re-add any rules you need by keeping ESLint as a project script and running it through vp run.
